audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers gave Ziggs levels 2, 3 and 6 at 2/10, while the whys beside them say level 2 is 'a wash', level 3 is 'skill-on-skill', 'You own 4-5' and 'You own 6 — this is your premier dive window'. The difficulty block is also self-contradictory: diff EVEN, diffRating 8.5/10, report[14] 'Hard matchup', against a 50.13% win rate.
audit.why: Level 3 gives Irelia a stun-into-reset all-in; 4-5 and 6 are her stick-and-kill window against a squishy artillery mage with one displacement on a 12-20s cooldown. Ziggs genuinely owns level 1 and 2+ items.
audit.corrected: Ziggs, Skill, Skill, Irelia, Irelia, Skill, Ziggs — matched pairs both layers, ratings rebuilt, difficulty brought to 6/10 to match the EVEN label and a 50.13% win rate.

audit.why: Spikes are right: Ziggs level 1 and late, Irelia at 3 and 6. Phase text now names Satchel Charge's 12s max-rank cooldown so the dive window is concrete.

audit.whatIsWrong: The mid section credits Irelia with 'armor/MR shred', which her kit does not have. Satchel Charge's real behaviour — a delayed charge that can be re-activated, knocking BOTH of them away — is never explained, and Short Fuse's auto-attack reset is absent.
audit.why: Riot text — Irelia P: stacking Attack Speed and bonus damage on hit, no resistance reduction. Ziggs W: 'flings an explosive charge that detonates after a delay, or when this ability is activated again... knocking them away. Ziggs is also knocked away, but takes no damage' (20/18/16/14/12s). Ziggs P Short Fuse: 'Periodically, Ziggs' next basic attack deals bonus magic damage. This cooldown is reduced whenever Ziggs uses an ability.'
audit.corrected: Max-stack Ionian Fervor on-hit damage, not shred. Satchel is a delayed or manually detonated charge that displaces both of them, 12s at max rank. Short Fuse's armed auto is a wind-up tell, and it comes back faster the more he casts.

edits.before: Q resets through minions are your engine — keep the wave healthy. Only take the trade when Ziggs's Satchel Charge is down.
edits.after: Defiant Dance soaks a bomb, but you still cannot reach him to punish — farm the wave and get to level 3 healthy.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Ziggs must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: E is online and gives you a real all-in, but Satchel Charge can fling him out of it — skill decides who commits first.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Satchel Charge's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Yours now: stacked Bladesurge and tighter cooldowns let you stick through the Satchel knockback and shred a squishy artillery mage.

edits.before: Vanguard’s Edge walls off his disengage and marks the kill. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Ziggs's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Yours: wall behind him with Vanguard's Edge so a 12s Satchel cannot fling him clear, then E-stun and run him down.

edits.before: Overall difficulty: 8.5/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Satchel Charge and how disciplined your pattern is.
edits.after: Overall difficulty: 6/10. Survive level 1, then own 3 through first item — the danger is letting it reach a siege.

edits.before: Hard matchup — difficulty 8.5/10, Ziggs carry threat 7.5/10.
edits.after: Even matchup — difficulty 6/10, Ziggs carry threat 7.5/10.

edits.before: His knockback + self-peel escape. Engage when it's down. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Satchel knocks both of you away, and it is down 12s at max rank — engage inside that gap.

edits.before: That is Ziggs's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Short Fuse arms a bonus-damage auto — the wind-up is the cue to step off.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Satchel detonates on a delay or on recast — it cancels your dive.

edits.before: This is your window. With your Bladesurge stacks building and E up, every time his W-Satchel is on cooldown you can E-stun and chain Q-resets through the wave to stick to him — and your max-stack on-hit plus armor/MR shred melts a squishy artillery mage fast. At 6, Vanguard's Edge answers his entire kit: drop the blade wall behind him so his W-Satchel displacement can't fling him to safety, then E-stun and run him down. Watch for his E minefield on the obvious dash lanes — path your Bladesurge through a different minion angle so you don't eat the slow mid-dive.

notes: Third instance in this slice of Irelia's passive being written as armour/MR shred — it is stacking attack speed plus bonus on-hit damage at max stacks, with no resistance reduction. Worth a champion-wide grep of champ-data/content/irelia.js for 'shred' by whoever owns the data. Difficulty block was self-contradictory (diff EVEN, rating 8.5/10, report line 'Hard') on a 50.13% win rate; brought to 6/10 and EVEN throughout. Satchel Charge displaces Ziggs too and can be manually detonated — both now stated.
